meta.title: AI Chat Interface
meta.description: A complete streaming chat UI. Thinking blocks, tool call display, markdown rendering, code highlighting, file attachments, message actions, model selector, and scroll anchoring — all wired.

blocks.content: Chat UIs fail at the edges. The first streaming token needs to update the UI immediately — a re-render per character, potentially hundreds of times per second. The scroll container needs to follow the bottom while the user watches, but stop when they scroll up and resume when they come back. An AbortController needs to be wired from the Stop button through to the fetch call. Tool calls need to transition pending → running → done without remounting. Thinking blocks need to stream in, then collapse.

AIChatRoot solves all of it. Pass onSend and receive a set of stream callbacks — appendToken, appendThinkingToken, addBlock, updateBlock, setStatus. Call them as your stream arrives and the UI updates live. Scroll anchoring, stop/cancel, and message state are handled automatically.

blocks.title: Model-agnostic by design
blocks.content: The system never calls any AI API. You bring onSend and call whatever provider you want — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, a local Ollama instance, or your own backend. The model selector is UI state that gets passed to your callback.
Click any conversation starter to trigger a simulated response. Watch the thinking block stream in, tool calls transition state, then the full markdown response arrive.

blocks.label: Interactive demo — all responses are simulated

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.code: npm install react-markdown remark-gfm sugar-high motion

blocks.content: Wrap your chat UI in AIChatRoot and pass onSend. The system renders the message list, typing indicator, and composer automatically. Your onSend receives the text and a set of stream callbacks — call them as tokens arrive.

blocks.title: Works with Vercel AI SDK
blocks.content: If you use useChat from the Vercel AI SDK, use controlled mode instead — pass messages and isLoading from useChat, and wire onSendControlled to append.
Pass messages, isLoading, and onSendControlled to take over message state yourself. Use this when you're integrating with an existing AI SDK that manages its own state.

Every message has content: AIContentBlock[] — an ordered array of blocks, not a single string. One response can contain a thinking block, a tool call, a paragraph of text, and a code snippet, all in sequence. Add blocks at any point during streaming with addBlock, and update them with updateBlock.

Thinking blocks stream character by character via appendThinkingToken — separate from the main text stream. They render as a collapsible panel with a pulsing brain icon while streaming, then collapse to a readable summary when done.
Thinking blocks default to expanded. The user can collapse them by clicking the header. Pass collapsed: true on the initial addBlock call to start collapsed.
Add a tool-call block when your model starts a function call, then update it as the call progresses. The component shows a spinner for pending and running, a check for done, and an X for error.

The Stop button calls stopGeneration which aborts the AbortController and marks the current streaming message as done. Pass the signal from AIStreamCallbacks to your fetch call — when aborted, fetch throws an AbortError which the root catches and handles cleanly.
